about: Free tiers and plans for compute, CI and AI inference, public fields only. Built by tools/catalog.py; every row names the vendor page it was read on and the date. verified: true means every figure was read on that first-party page on that date; false means it was not re-read since.

rows.name: Blacksmith free tier
rows.price_note: Free minutes each month, then pay as you go.
rows.includes: 3,000 x64 2vCPU minutes per month per organization. ARM, Windows, macOS and larger runners draw these down at conversion rates: 1 ARM 2vCPU minute = 0.625, 1 Windows 2vCPU minute = 2, and macOS uses a 6.67 price ratio with a 6 vCPU minimum.
rows.unit_cost_vs_payg: Paid per minute: Ubuntu x64 $0.004, Ubuntu ARM $0.0025, Windows x64 $0.008, macOS M4 $0.08. Docker layer caching and sticky disks are $0.50/GB per month; static IPs are $100/IP per month.
rows.limits: Blacksmith docs state no concurrency limit on jobs or vCPUs. The pages do not say what happens when the free minutes run out.

rows.name: GitHub Enterprise Cloud (included Actions)
rows.price_note: USD per user per month. The pricing page says Enterprise now includes access to GitHub Copilot.
rows.includes: $300 per month of included Actions compute, which covers 50,000 Linux 2-core minutes at $0.006 (pricing page: 50,000 CI/CD minutes per month). 50 GB artifact storage, 10 GB cache per repository, 150 GB custom image storage. Larger runners, the GPU runner among them, can draw from the included amount.
rows.unit_cost_vs_payg: Past $300: Linux 2-core x64 $0.006/min, Linux 2-core arm64 $0.005/min, Linux 4-core GPU $0.052/min. Storage past the allowance: $0.25 per GB-month for artifacts and Packages, $0.07 for cache, $0.07 for custom image storage.
rows.limits: Past the included amount, usage bills the payment method on file. A budget set to stop usage can block Actions spend. Without a valid payment method, usage is blocked once included compute is used. Standard GitHub-hosted runners: 500 concurrent jobs, at most 50 macOS jobs.

rows.name: GitHub Actions on GitHub Free
rows.price_note: GitHub Free plan. GitHub Pro is a paid plan with a larger allowance.
rows.includes: Private repositories: $12 of included compute per month on GitHub Free (also GitHub Free for organizations), with 500 MB artifact storage and 10 GB cache per repository. GitHub Pro gets $18 and 1 GB. At $0.006 per Linux 2-core minute, $12 covers 2,000 minutes and $18 covers 3,000 (computed here; github.com/pricing also shows 2,000 CI/CD minutes on Free). Cloud sandbox compute and memory now draw from the same included amount. Standard GitHub-hosted runners in public repositories, GitHub Pages and Dependabot are free and do not draw on the allowance.
rows.unit_cost_vs_payg: Per minute: Linux 1-core $0.002, Linux 2-core x64 $0.006, Linux 2-core arm64 $0.005, Windows 2-core x64 $0.010, Windows 2-core arm64 $0.010, macOS 3 or 4-core $0.062. Extra storage $0.25 per GB-month (artifacts and Packages), $0.07 per GB-month (cache).
rows.limits: 6 hours per job and 35 days per workflow run. 20 concurrent jobs on Free (40 on Pro), with at most 5 macOS jobs. Without a payment method, usage is blocked once the included amount is used. With a payment method on file, extra usage bills unless a budget stops it; the page states no default $0 budget.

rows.name: AWS Free plan
rows.price_note: Free plan: no charges unless you upgrade to the Paid plan or activate paid-only services. New customers on the Paid plan also get up to $200 in credits.
rows.includes: $100 in credits at sign-up plus up to $100 more earned by completing activities with foundational services (up to $200), usable for up to 6 months. Free plan is limited to select services (the page says over 90). Separately, 30+ services have Always Free monthly limits on both Free and Paid plans.
rows.unit_cost_vs_payg: $0 within credit
rows.limits: The Free plan ends 6 months after account creation or when credits run out, whichever comes first, and cannot be extended. AWS then suspends the account; data is kept 90 days, during which an upgrade to the Paid plan restores access, after which the account and content are erased. Usage past Always Free limits is paid from credits; once credits are exhausted you must upgrade. Paid plan: spend limit from $20 per project can pause resources. Accounts that already had an AWS account are not eligible. The FAQ gives two different credit expiry periods after an upgrade (12 months in one answer, 6 months in another).

rows.name: Claude Code on the web (cloud sessions)
rows.price_note: No separate charge for the cloud VM. Needs a paid plan: Pro is $20 billed monthly, or $17 per month on an annual subscription ($200 billed up front) (claude.com/pricing). Usage counts toward the plan's limits.
rows.includes: One isolated Anthropic-managed VM per session, Ubuntu 24.04 on x86_64, with approximate ceilings of 4 vCPUs, 16 GB RAM and 30 GB disk that may change over time. The docs list no GPU. Available on Pro, Max, Ultra and Team plans, and to Enterprise users with premium or Chat + Claude Code seats.
rows.unit_cost_vs_payg: No per-VM charge. Usage draws on the plan's usage limits.
rows.limits: Cloud sessions share rate limits with all other Claude and Claude Code usage. Network access has three levels (None, Limited, Full); the default is Limited with 'Allow package managers' checked, and environments saved as the former 'Trusted' level open as Limited. Foreground commands wait 2 minutes by default (up to 10); a command moved to the background runs up to 30 more minutes. After a few minutes without activity the VM pauses with files saved, and a paused VM can later be reclaimed. GitHub is needed to clone and push from GitHub, but a repository with no GitHub remote can be bundled from the terminal and uploaded (bundle under 100 MB). Members governed by custom roles need the cloud sessions permission. Organizations with Zero Data Retention, HIPAA configuration or customer-managed keys cannot use cloud sessions.

rows.unit_cost_vs_payg: $150 per concurrent slot
rows.limits: Concurrency equals the number of runners bought; workflows labelled low-priority yield to regular ones near the concurrency limit. Subscription can be changed at any time.

rows.name: Cloudflare Workers Paid

rows.unit_cost_vs_payg: $0.30 per additional million requests. $0.02 per additional million CPU milliseconds. Requests to static assets are free.
rows.limits: CPU time up to 5 minutes per request (default 30 seconds). Cron Triggers: up to 5 minutes CPU (default 30 seconds) for intervals under 1 hour, 15 minutes for intervals of 1 hour or more. Queue consumers: 15 minutes wall time per invocation. 128 MB memory per Worker isolate. On Free, requests past 100,000 a day get Error 1027.

rows.limits: Without a valid payment method, usage is blocked once the included compute is used. Concurrent jobs depend on the GitHub plan.

Cloud Run (request-based billing): 2 million requests, 360,000 GB-seconds of memory and 180,000 vCPU-seconds per month. Cloud Build: 2,500 build-minutes per month on e2-standard-2.

rows.name: Google Colab (free of charge version)
rows.price_note: Free. Colab Pro, Pro+ and Pay As You Go are paid options using compute units.
rows.includes: Free access to computing resources including GPUs and TPUs, with no guarantee. GPU and TPU types vary over time, and access to expensive GPUs is heavily restricted. Notebooks run at most 12 hours, depending on availability and usage patterns. Standard system memory profile.
rows.limits: Idle runtimes time out. Without a positive compute unit balance, free runtimes may be terminated without warning for SSH shells or remote desktops, bypassing the notebook UI to work through a web UI, chess training, or distributed computing workers. All managed runtimes bar file hosting, media serving, remote proxies, torrents, crypto mining, password cracking and deepfakes. Colab terms bar selling or providing access to Colab to third parties.

rows.name: Google Colab Pro
rows.price_note: US price per month.
rows.includes: 100 compute units per month. Compute units expire after 90 days. Faster GPUs and high-memory machines, subject to availability.
rows.unit_cost_vs_payg: $0.0999 per compute unit, the same as Pay As You Go (100 units for $9.99). Google publishes no per-GPU unit burn rate on the pages read.
rows.limits: GPU type and availability are not guaranteed. Notebooks run at most 12 hours. At zero units, paid users revert to free-tier rules. Connecting to remote proxies is disallowed on all managed runtimes. Web UIs that bypass the notebook are disallowed only without a positive unit balance.

rows.name: Google Colab Pro+
rows.price_note: US price per month.
rows.includes: 600 compute units per month (Pro's 100 plus an additional 500), faster GPUs, highest-memory machines, background execution. Compute units expire after 90 days.
rows.unit_cost_vs_payg: About $0.083 per compute unit ($49.99 / 600, derived) vs $0.0999 on Pay As You Go ($49.99 per 500). Google publishes no per-GPU compute-unit burn rate on the pages read.
rows.limits: Pro+ supports continuous code execution for up to 24 hours with sufficient compute units. GPU types and availability are not guaranteed.

rows.name: GPU Mart RTX A6000 server
rows.includes: RTX A6000 48 GB, 2x 18-core E5-2697v4, 256 GB RAM, 240 GB SSD + 2 TB NVMe + 8 TB SATA, 100 Mbps unmetered, 1 IPv4, USA.
rows.unit_cost_vs_payg: $0.56/h at 730 h vs $0.33 RunPod

rows.name: Hetzner GEX45
rows.price_note: EUR 214.00 per month or EUR 0.3429 per hour, excl. VAT, plus EUR 209.00 one-time setup fee.
rows.includes: NVIDIA RTX PRO 4000 Blackwell SFF 24 GB, Intel Core i5-13500, 64 GB DDR4, 2x 512 GB NVMe; EUR 209 setup; unlimited traffic.
rows.unit_cost_vs_payg: EUR 0.29/h at 730 h (derived) or EUR 0.3429/h on hourly billing, vs $0.34 RunPod Community RTX 4090 (read today).

rows.name: Hetzner GEX63
rows.price_note: EUR 999.00 per month or EUR 1.6009 per hour, excl. VAT, plus EUR 999.00 one-time setup fee.
rows.includes: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q 96 GB, Intel Core Ultra 7 265, 128 GB DDR5, 2x 1.92 TB NVMe; EUR 999 setup; unlimited traffic.
rows.unit_cost_vs_payg: EUR 1.37/h at 730 h (derived) or EUR 1.6009/h on hourly billing, vs $1.69 RunPod Community RTX Pro 6000 (read today).

rows.name: Hot Aisle MI300X
rows.includes: MI300X 192 GB VMs (1x, 2x, 4x) $2.99/GPU-h billed by the minute; 8x bare metal $3.39/GPU-h. 1x VM: 8 or 13 CPU cores, 224 GB RAM, 12 TB NVMe.
rows.unit_cost_vs_payg: $2.99 vs $2.59 DO AMD
rows.limits: Quick start flow: create a team, add credits, then provision.

rows.name: Hugging Face PRO
rows.price_note: Per personal account per month.
rows.includes: 40 minutes per day of ZeroGPU quota (8x the free account's 5 minutes) on the default half NVIDIA RTX Pro 6000 Blackwell (48 GB). The xlarge size (full card, 96 GB) uses quota at 2x. Host up to 10 ZeroGPU Spaces. $2 per month of compute credits, usable on Inference Providers, Inference Endpoints, Spaces hardware, ZeroGPU past quota and Jobs.
rows.unit_cost_vs_payg: About 20 GPU-hours per month at 48 GB, or 10 at 96 GB (derived: 40 min x 30 days). That is $0.45 or $0.90 per GPU-hour (derived). Past quota, ZeroGPU costs $1 per 10 minutes ($6 per hour) from prepaid credits.
rows.limits: Past the daily quota, usage draws prepaid credits automatically when the balance is positive; with no balance it stops. Quota resets 24 hours after first GPU use. ZeroGPU Spaces work with the Gradio SDK only.

rows.name: Hugging Face Team
rows.price_note: Per user per month, paid by credit card.
rows.includes: Every member gets PRO ZeroGPU and Inference Providers benefits: 40 minutes per day of ZeroGPU quota each. $2 per seat per month of compute credits, shared across the organization. The organization can host up to 50 ZeroGPU Spaces. SSO, audit logs, resource groups and storage regions.
rows.unit_cost_vs_payg: Same per-member ZeroGPU quota as PRO at $20 instead of $9 (2.2x). Past quota, $1 per 10 minutes from prepaid credits. Enterprise ($500 per user per month on the pricing page) gives 60 minutes per day.
rows.limits: Team credits apply only when a request names the organization to bill. Past quota, usage draws prepaid credits when the balance is positive.

rows.name: Hugging Face ZeroGPU (free account)
rows.price_note: Free account. PRO, Team and Enterprise get larger quotas.
rows.includes: 5 minutes of ZeroGPU time per day on a free account (2 minutes unauthenticated) across any ZeroGPU Space. Default size is half an NVIDIA RTX Pro 6000 Blackwell with 48 GB VRAM; xlarge (full card, 96 GB) uses quota at 2x. A free personal account in good standing (verified email, older than 30 days) can host up to 2 ZeroGPU Spaces.
rows.unit_cost_vs_payg: PRO, Team and Enterprise users can continue past the daily quota with pre-paid credits at $1 per 10 minutes of GPU time. Free accounts have no such option.
rows.limits: ZeroGPU Spaces work only with the Gradio SDK. Default GPU time per call is 60 seconds, settable with a duration argument. torch.compile is not supported. Free accounts get medium queue priority. The quota resets 24 hours after first GPU use.

rows.name: Hyperstack reserved
rows.unit_cost_vs_payg: RTX PRO 6000 $1.30 vs $1.69 RunPod
rows.limits: Reservations are invoiced monthly; on-demand is prepaid and billed per minute. Payment by credit card via Stripe. The pricing page carries a banner warning of a fraudulent website impersonating Hyperstack at hyperstack.my (no start date given).

rows.name: Kaggle Notebooks (free GPU quota)
rows.price_note: Free. Kaggle states no paid notebook tier.
rows.includes: Weekly GPU quota of 30 hours, or sometimes higher depending on demand and resources. GPU choices: 1 NVIDIA Tesla P100 (4 CPU cores, 29 GB RAM) or 2 NVIDIA Tesla T4 (4 CPU cores, 29 GB RAM). Each session runs up to 12 hours (9 hours on TPU) with 20 GB of auto-saved disk. CPU sessions get 4 cores and 30 GB RAM.
rows.unit_cost_vs_payg: No pay-as-you-go rate stated. A limited-time promotion gives linked Colab Pro and Pro+ subscribers 15 and 30 extra GPU hours per week.
rows.limits: 12-hour execution cap per session (9 hours for TPU). Interactive sessions stay active until a 60-minute idle timeout. Kaggle Terms limit use to internal, personal, non-commercial use, not on behalf of any third party.

rows.name: Lambda on-demand instances
rows.price_note: Per GPU-hour, billed by the minute, weekly invoices. Prices exclude sales tax.
rows.unit_cost_vs_payg: A6000 $1.09 is 3.3x RunPod Community's $0.33 (both read today).
rows.limits: Only major credit cards are accepted (prepaid and debit cards are declined), with a $10 pre-authorization. Instances bill while running, used or not. No free credit or subscription found. Purchases only from a listed set of countries.

rows.name: machine.dev GPU runners for GitHub Actions
rows.includes: Credits at $0.005 each. Builder $25/mo = $25, Developer $50 = $55, Growth $85 = $100, Pro $160 = $200, Business $300 = $375; one-time $20 bundle; $10 free trial (about 45 GPU-hours on T4G spot).
rows.unit_cost_vs_payg: About $0.22/h for T4G spot (derived from the page's '$10 ... ~45 GPU hours'). Plan bonuses are 10-25% extra credit.
rows.limits: Credits roll over every month and never expire. Plans can be upgraded or switched at any time.

rows.name: Modal Starter
rows.price_note: $0 plus compute per month. Usage beyond the included credit is pay as you go.
rows.includes: $30 per month of included compute (GPU, CPU, memory) for Functions and Sandboxes. 3 workspace seats, 100 containers, 10 GPU concurrency, 200 deployed apps, 5 deployed crons, 1-day log retention and 1 TiB per month of free egress. Model APIs (per-token, formerly called Shared Endpoints in the catalog) are not covered and bill from the first request (since September 1, 2026).
rows.unit_cost_vs_payg: Per second: RTX PRO 6000 $0.000842, L40S $0.000542, L4 $0.000222, T4 $0.000164, H100 SXM5 $0.001097. At those rates $30 buys about 9.9 h of RTX PRO 6000, 15.4 h of L40S or 37.5 h of L4 (computed here, not stated by Modal).
rows.limits: 10 GPU concurrency and 100 containers. Using a GPU requires a valid payment method on file. A workspace spend limit caps out-of-pocket charges and stops workloads at the cap; the default spend limit is the cycle's usage limit minus credits. Environment-level budgets are Team and Enterprise only.

rows.name: Modal Team
rows.price_note: $250 per month plus compute. Unlimited seats.
rows.includes: $100 per month of included compute, 50 GPU concurrency, 5,000 containers, 1,000 deployed apps, 10 TiB per month egress, 30-day log retention, custom domains.
rows.unit_cost_vs_payg: Compute is pay-as-you-go by the second: H100 SXM5 $0.001097/s ($3.95/h), RTX PRO 6000 $0.000842/s ($3.03/h), A100 80 GB $0.000694/s ($2.50/h), L40S $0.000542/s ($1.95/h), T4 $0.000164/s ($0.59/h). The plan costs $150 per month more than its included credit (derived).
rows.limits: A workspace budget can cap monthly spend. Included usage does not cover Model APIs, which bill per token from the first request. Starter ($0) has $30 per month included, 3 seats and 10 GPU concurrency.

rows.name: RunComfy Pro
rows.price_note: $29.99 billed monthly, or $19.99 per month billed yearly ($239.92 per year).
rows.includes: 20%+ off all GPU rates (ComfyUI and Trainer), $10 credit added each month, 20 CPU hours per month, 200 GB storage with permanent retention, unlimited saved workflow environments.
rows.unit_cost_vs_payg: X-Large A6000 48 GB $1.99/h on Pro vs $2.50 pay as you go; RunPod Community RTX A6000 $0.33 (read today).
rows.limits: Purchased funds expire 365 days after purchase. A balance is still needed with Pro; usage is pay-as-you-go from it.

rows.name: RunPod Community Cloud (on-demand)
rows.price_note: Prepaid balance, rates shown per hour and per second. Deploying a Pod needs at least one hour's worth of credits.
rows.unit_cost_vs_payg: Baseline. Secure Cloud costs more: RTX A6000 $0.69, RTX Pro 6000 $2.69, H200 $5.29, B200 $7.99 per hour.
rows.limits: At a $0 balance RunPod stops all running Pods. Pods without a network volume are terminated and their data is lost. Network volume storage keeps billing while Pods are stopped. Default spend limit $80 per hour. Prepaid cards should deposit at least $100.

rows.name: SaladCloud GPU
rows.price_note: Per GPU-hour by priority tier (Lowest to High), billed per second while running; vCPU and RAM included.
rows.includes: RTX 3090 $0.09-0.20, RTX 4090 $0.16-0.44, RTX 5090 $0.25-0.60 per GPU-hour (Lowest to High priority), vCPU and RAM included.
rows.unit_cost_vs_payg: Lowest tier x 730 h: RTX 5090 $182.50/month, RTX 4090 $116.80, RTX 3090 $65.70. RunPod Community RTX 4090 $0.34/h (read today).
rows.limits: No free trial. Lower priority tiers can be preempted by higher ones; Lowest is the most interruptible.

rows.name: Saturn Cloud free
rows.includes: A free account (Hosted Free) to try the platform. The page says to upgrade to Hosted Pro 'to unlock resource usage capabilities'. No free compute hours, GPU or RAM amounts are stated.
rows.limits: Hosted Pro: $5 up-front credit charge, then the card is charged every $10 of usage. Saturn Cloud's own price is $0.00/hour; you pay the hosting price (e.g. Nebius 1x H100 $2.95/h, AWS T4 g4dn.xlarge $0.53/h).

rows.name: ThinkDiffusion TD-Pro
rows.price_note: $29.99 billed monthly, or $19.99 per month billed yearly.
rows.includes: $10 monthly balance credit (unused credits roll over), 20% off machine rates, 200 GB private drive with persistent storage. ULTRA 48 GB $1.99/h (standard $2.50).
rows.unit_cost_vs_payg: ULTRA 48 GB $1.99/h on TD-Pro vs $2.50 standard; RunPod Community RTX A6000 $0.33 (read today).

rows.name: Thunder Compute
rows.includes: On-demand instances billed per minute while running, at these hourly rates: RTX A6000 $0.35, L40 $0.79, A100 80GB $1.09, H100 SXM $3.20 per GPU-hour. Extra vCPU $0.04/vCPU-hr; instance disk beyond the first 100 GB per GPU $0.219/GB-month; snapshots $0.05/GB-month; no egress fees. Sandboxes (per-second billing, access by request): H100 SXM $2.95, A100 80GB $1.95 per GPU-hour.
rows.unit_cost_vs_payg: Thunder's own comparison table (on-demand list prices checked Nov 22, 2026): H100 $3.20 vs Lambda $3.79, Runpod $4.39, AWS $6.88 per GPU-hour. These are the vendor's claims about competitors.
rows.limits: Instances and sandboxes are never preempted. Reserved and volume pricing are by sales quote.

rows.name: Vast.ai reserved
rows.includes: Reserved: 1, 3 or 6-month terms, up to 50% off, guaranteed capacity, volume discounts; the pricing page sends reservations to Contact Sales. Interruptible: 50%+ cheaper than on-demand, may be reclaimed. Per-second billing; prices set by supply and demand.
rows.unit_cost_vs_payg: Up to 50% off on-demand marketplace rates (vendor's wording). Live rates vary; no fixed reserved price is published.

rows.name: Verda (ex-DataCrunch) spot
rows.unit_cost_vs_payg: Spot is half of Verda's own on-demand price (B200 $4.874 vs $9.747; H200 $3.522 vs $7.043; A100 80GB $1.235 vs $2.470).

rows.name: OpenCode Go
rows.price_note: $10 a month for Go. Go Plus is $40 a month. Go Teams is $20 per member per month with a 2-member minimum ($40 a month).
rows.includes: One monthly allowance shared by all paid models. Each model's monthly limit (the amount covered if you use only that model) runs from $15 to $200 at OpenCode's token prices: for example Claude Haiku 5.5, GPT 6 Luna, Grok 4.7 and Kimi K3 at $15, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash at $100, GLM-5.3 at $200. Models include Claude Haiku 5.5, GPT 6 Luna, GPT 5.6 Luna, Gemini 4 Argon, Grok 4.7, and open models (GLM, Kimi, Qwen, MiniMax, MiMo, DeepSeek, Hy, Step, LongCat, Muse Spark Contributor). The 5-hour limit is 20% and the weekly limit 50% of the monthly allowance; the weekly limit resets Monday 00:00 UTC.
rows.unit_cost_vs_payg: Claude Haiku 5.5 costs $0.10/$0.50 per M, the same as Anthropic's list price, with a $15 limit. Per-model limits run from 1.5x to 20x the $10 fee (computed). Gemini 4 Argon is 50% off through November 30, 2026. DeepSeek models cost 2x on weekdays from 01:00 to 04:00 and 06:00 to 10:00 UTC.
rows.limits: At a limit you can keep using the free models, or opt in to Extra Usage, which draws on a Console pay-as-you-go balance (Go Teams starts with Extra Usage on). Default regions are Europe and United States. DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, DeepSeek V4 Pro and LongCat 2.5 (hosted in China) need the Global region. Muse Spark Contributor models need 'Allow paid endpoints that train on request data'. Workspaces with no saved privacy settings also allow Global for requests from China. Clients should send x-opencode-session and their own user agent. Terms allow your own internal use only. Trap: save the privacy settings with Global off and the training toggle off.

rows.name: Claude API prepaid credits (Claude Console)
rows.price_note: No subscription. Prepaid usage credits bought in the Claude Console; billed per token at list price.
rows.includes: Per million tokens, input/output: Haiku 5.5 $0.10/$0.50 for prompts up to 100K tokens and $0.50/$2.50 above; Sonnet 5.5 $2/$10; Opus 5.5 $4/$20; Fable 5.2 $8/$40 (Fable 5.1 is still $10/$50). Batch API halves input and output prices.
rows.unit_cost_vs_payg: List price. Batch API is 50 percent off; US-only inference costs 1.1x; fast mode costs 2x (Opus 5.5 $8/$40, Fable 5.2 $16/$80).
rows.limits: Bought credits expire one year after purchase and cannot be extended or refunded. When credits run out the API stops until you add more; auto-reload is optional. Rate limits depend on the account's usage tier (not read here).

rows.name: ArliAI Core (Plus $20, Pro $30)
rows.price_note: Core $15, Plus $20, Pro $30 and Max $160 a month; 10% off when paid annually.
rows.includes: Core: unlimited tokens and requests, 1 request at a time, standard priority, models up to 552B, 32K context, image generation up to 3 MP. Plus: 128K context. Pro: 2 parallel requests, high priority, 256K context. Max: 6 parallel requests, 512K context.
rows.unit_cost_vs_payg: Flat
rows.limits: The page headline says 'Unlimited. Zero-Log. Monthly Pricing.' Core is limited to 32K context and 1 request at a time.

rows.name: AssemblyAI free credit
rows.includes: Up to $50 of audio on a limited trial: pre-recorded transcription, Speech Understanding and streaming speech-to-text. LLM Gateway is not on the free tier.
rows.limits: Once the $50 is used, the API returns an error until you add a card and upgrade.

rows.name: Cerebras Inference Free Trial
rows.price_note: One-time $5 promotional credit; there is no permanently free tier.
rows.includes: $5 in credits after adding a verified payment method, valid 30 days, usable on every Shared Inference model. Free Trial limits: gpt-oss-120b 5 RPM, 30K uncached TPM, 90K total TPM, 1M tokens per hour and 1M tokens per day. qwen-3.8-27b 300 RPM, 150K uncached TPM, 750K total TPM (temporarily raised from 450K), no hourly or daily token caps, the same as Pay as You Go.
rows.unit_cost_vs_payg: Pay as you go credits after the trial; rates not read here.
rows.limits: Without a payment method, Playground and API access stay inactive. Access pauses when the credit expires or runs out. The pricing page says the tier is for development, evaluation and experimentation, not production.

rows.name: Chutes Plus (Pro $20)
rows.price_note: ENDED. Monthly plans are no longer sold. Existing plans stay active to the end of the current billing period, do not renew, and then bill pay-as-you-go from the account balance. Chutes offers no free tier.
rows.includes: Offer ended. Chutes now sells only pay-per-token inference (for example Qwen3.8-27B-TEE $0.039 input and $1.25 output per M) and Private Chutes on TEE GPUs (RTX Pro 6000 $2.25 an hour plus a one-time deploy fee of 3x the hourly rate).
rows.unit_cost_vs_payg: 6% (Pro 10%) off PAYG
rows.limits: Pay-as-you-go from a prepaid account balance, with no subscription and no minimum. Volume pricing is by sales quote.

rows.name: Cloudflare AI Search (formerly AutoRAG)
rows.price_note: No separate subscription. AI Search billing begins December 1, 2026. Each account gets included usage every month on Workers Free and Workers Paid; usage past it is metered.
rows.includes: Monthly: 5 million ingestion tokens (image-processing tokens share this allotment), 10 GB-month storage, 1,000 semantic queries, 1,000 full-text queries. OCR is available on every account and bills as image-processing tokens. Workers AI embedding and reranking, R2, Vectorize and Browser Run crawling done for AI Search are included in AI Search usage. Generation, query rewriting, file summaries and external models bill through Workers AI or AI Gateway.
rows.unit_cost_vs_payg: Ingestion $0.75 per M tokens (images add $0.50 per M); storage $2.00 per GB-month; semantic, vector or hybrid queries $0.75 per 1,000; full-text queries $0.10 per 1,000; instances past 5,000 on Paid $0.10 a month each.
rows.limits: Workers Free: 100 instances, 100,000 files per instance, 500 crawled pages a day. Workers Paid: 5,000 instances by default, 1M files per instance (500K for hybrid search), no daily crawl cap. Both: 100 namespaces, 10 MiB max for OCR PDFs and text files, 4 MiB for other formats, 100,000 pages per discover crawl. A legacy R2 crawl bucket can still bill R2 storage.

rows.name: Cloudflare Workers AI free daily allocation
rows.price_note: Free on both Workers plans, Free and Paid. Usage above it needs Workers Paid, where it bills.
rows.includes: 10,000 Neurons per day. At the page's rates that is about 314K gpt-oss-120b input tokens (31,818 Neurons per million) or about 96 FLUX.2 Klein 4B 1024x1024 outputs (4 output tiles at 26.05 Neurons each).
rows.unit_cost_vs_payg: Workers Paid only: $0.011 per 1,000 Neurons above 10,000 per day. Workers Free has no overage option.
rows.limits: Limits reset at 00:00 UTC. On Workers Free, use past the allocation fails with an error. On Workers Paid, it bills at $0.011 per 1,000 Neurons. Nine models (two Kimi, three GLM, three DeepSeek and Inkling 2 Small) require a paid billing method: Workers Paid or prepaid AI Gateway credits.

rows.name: Cloudflare Workers AI past the free allocation
rows.price_note: Needs the Workers Paid plan, minimum $5 a month per account, then usage. Prepaid AI Gateway credits are an alternative way to pay.
rows.includes: 10,000 Neurons a day free on both Workers plans. Past that, Workers Paid bills $0.011 per 1,000 Neurons. Example LLM rates: gpt-oss-120b $0.350 input and $0.750 output per M tokens; llama-3.3-70b-instruct-fp8-fast $0.293 and $2.253.
rows.unit_cost_vs_payg: $0.011 per 1,000 Neurons, shown per model as per-token prices.
rows.limits: On Workers Free, requests past 10,000 Neurons a day fail with an error until 00:00 UTC. Text generation defaults to 300 requests per minute. The nine models that need a paid billing method (Kimi, GLM, DeepSeek, Inkling) instead get 20 requests per minute per model, or 50 with prepaid AI Gateway credits on Unified billing.

rows.name: ElevenLabs Creator
rows.price_note: $22 a month; annual billing $18.33 a month. Black Friday until December 1, 2026: $8.25 a month for the first year on annual billing ($99 for the year). The FAQ also lists $11 for the first month.
rows.includes: 121,000 credits a month (about 121 minutes of text to speech), Professional Voice Cloning, 30 custom voice slots, 5 concurrent requests, 128 and 192 kbps audio.
rows.limits: 5 concurrent requests. Unused credits roll over for up to two months (balance up to 3x the monthly quota) while subscribed. PAYG top-ups start at $5, expire 12 months after purchase and are non-refundable.

rows.name: ElevenLabs Free
rows.price_note: $0 per month.
rows.includes: 10,000 credits per month, about 10 minutes of text to speech (1 credit per character on V2 Multilingual). 3 Studio projects.
rows.unit_cost_vs_payg: Free; paid plans start with Starter at $6 per month for 30,000 credits.
rows.limits: Non-commercial use only, with a personal email address. No credit rollover on Free. Content may be used for training unless you opt out. Optional PAYG top-ups (minimum $5) work on Free and raise concurrency to the Starter level (3), but voice slots and other plan limits stay at the Free level.

rows.name: ElevenLabs Starter
rows.price_note: $6 a month; annual billing $5 a month (monthly price times 10 per year). The page still shows a 'First month for $1' banner, but it is marked 'Ends September 30', so that promotion has lapsed.
rows.includes: 30,000 credits a month (about 30 minutes of text to speech), commercial license, Instant Voice Cloning, 20 Studio projects, 10 custom voice slots, 3 concurrent requests.
rows.unit_cost_vs_payg: The pricing table lists about $0.20 per extra minute for Starter. Pay-as-you-go top-ups start at $5 and expire 12 months after purchase.
rows.limits: 3 concurrent requests. Unused credits roll over for up to two months (balance up to 3x the monthly quota) while subscribed. Usage-based billing is not offered to new self-serve customers; service pauses at a zero top-up balance unless Auto Top Up is on.

rows.name: Featherless Chat
rows.includes: Unlimited tokens, 4 concurrent, 32K context
rows.unit_cost_vs_payg: Flat, but human use only
rows.limits: Interactive, human-driven use by the purchaser only: no reselling, app or API traffic, background automation or benchmarking. Misuse may lead to cancellation without refund. 40,000+ open models. Prompts and completions are never stored. Billed monthly; cancel any time. Switching to Developer mid-period forfeits the rest of the period.

rows.name: Featherless Developer
rows.price_note: From $50 a month (credit amount selectable), billed per token.
rows.includes: $50 or more of metered credits a month, context up to 256K, 100 concurrent units, 1 agent environment included, priority capacity.
rows.unit_cost_vs_payg: 1x (no discount)
rows.limits: Credits never expire and carry into later cycles. One-off top-ups any time. Only successful requests are billed. Requests are blocked at zero credit. Prompts are never stored. No reselling.

rows.name: Fireworks Fire Pass
rows.price_note: CLOSED TO NEW SUBSCRIPTIONS. Fire Pass is experimental and not open to new subscriptions; only existing users and promo recipients can manage a pass. No price is published.
rows.includes: Covered usage on enabled open-weight routers while the pass is active. kimi-fast-latest currently resolves to Kimi K3 Fast (1,040,000-token context, up to 131,072 output tokens), at $0 per token. Uses a dedicated fpk_ key.
rows.unit_cost_vs_payg: Flat (was $7/week, 3p)
rows.limits: Personal, non-production agentic coding only. No Responses API (Codex, ChatGPT desktop), no auto or Nexus Auto, and Nexus CLI rejects Fire Pass keys. Violations may revoke the pass.

rows.name: Gemini API Free tier
rows.price_note: Free input and output tokens on selected models; the Paid tier is pay as you go.
rows.includes: Free of charge on the Free tier: Gemini 4 Hydrogen, Gemini 3.8 Flash, 3.6 Flash, 3.5 Flash-Lite, 3.1 Flash-Lite, 3 Flash Preview, 2.5 Pro and 2.5 Flash (both deprecated), 2.5 Flash-Lite, Gemma 4, Gemini Embedding and Embedding 2, Gemini Decision 1, Robotics ER 2 previews, and the TTS, Live, Live Translate and Transcribe models. Not on the Free tier: Gemini 4 Carbon, 4 Argon, 4 Neon, Genie 4, Omni 1.2/1.1 Flash, 3.1 Pro Preview, the Nano Banana image models, 2.5 Pro Preview TTS, and Lyria 3/3.5.
rows.unit_cost_vs_payg: Free
rows.limits: Rate limits are per project and shown in AI Studio, not on the docs page. Daily quotas reset at midnight Pacific time. Apps made available to users in the EEA, Switzerland or the UK must use Paid Services. Free-tier content can be read by human reviewers. DEPRECATION: gemini-2.5-pro and gemini-2.5-flash are no longer selectable in AI Studio. From December 1, 2026, API calls to them route to gemini-3.8-flash and gemini-3.5-flash-lite respectively and bill at those rates.

rows.name: Groq Developer tier (pay as you go)
rows.price_note: No monthly fee. Pay per token, invoiced monthly in arrears, with early invoices when lifetime usage first crosses $1, $10, $100, $500 and $1,000.
